name: Luxembourg

train.sum: Luxembourg station (Gare Centrale) is the one main station for CFL trains. Since 1 March 2020, 2nd class travel on all trains inside Luxembourg is free for everyone, tourists included. Only 1st class and journeys across the border need a ticket.
train.sched: Trains to Trier, Metz and Brussels run about every hour, to Liege about every 2 hours, and to Paris about 5 times a day by TGV. Check the CFL app or mobiliteit.lu for exact times.
tickets: 2nd class inside Luxembourg: no ticket needed
1st class: 3 EUR for 2 hours, 6 EUR for a day, 10 two-hour tickets 24 EUR, monthly pass 60 EUR. 1st class tickets are not valid on international lines
Cross-border 2nd class is free up to the border, and also to Athus (Belgium), Audun-le-Tiche and Volmerange-les-Mines (France)
Examples abroad: Thionville 3.90 EUR, Arlon 4.60 EUR, Trier 5.40 EUR (2nd class), Brussels from about 21 EUR
Paris by TGV INOUI: about 2 h 10 min, price changes by date. Seat reservation is compulsory
train.tip: Free means 2nd class only. If you sit in a 1st class coach without a 1st class ticket, you can be fined 150 EUR. Carry an ID, because staff can ask for it.
buy: Nothing to buy for 2nd class trains inside Luxembourg
CFL go app, CFL International App and the CFL website
Ticket machines at stations and CFL counters. Sales centres at Luxembourg station and Belval-University, phone +352 2489 2489
Buy 1st class tickets before you board
Cross-border: you must show a valid ticket, checks start at the last stop in Luxembourg before the border
TGV and TER to France: SNCF Connect or station counters

destinations.note: Direct trains run many times an hour
On the Moselle at the German border
Northern line via Ettelbruck and Clervaux
Free in 2nd class on the Luxembourg side, then a ticket
One to five trains an hour
5 direct trains a day, reservation compulsory
About every hour via Arlon and Namur. No catering on board
TGV via Metz, Strasbourg and Lyon

tram.sum: The Luxtram line T1 runs about 16 km from Stadion through the centre to Kirchberg and Luxembourg Airport, with 24 stops. Trams, buses and the funicular are all free, so no ticket is needed.
tram.sched: Trams run every 3 to 8 minutes in the daytime. Check mobiliteit.lu for first and last tram times.
tickets: No ticket needed on the tram, on city buses or on the funicular
Pets travel free and there is no charge for luggage
Children under 4 must be with someone aged 12 or older
You can ride the whole line, including the airport, for free
tram.tip: Take the tram from Gare Centrale to Hamilius for the old town, or on to Kirchberg for the European institutions and Philharmonie. Carry your ID in case staff ask.
buy: Nothing to buy: public transport in Luxembourg is free
Nothing to validate and no gates
Plan trips with the Mobiliteit.lu app or website

bus.sum: City buses (AVL) and national RGTR buses are free. RGTR buses also cross the border to Germany, France and Belgium. Nightrider buses run at weekends after the regular service ends.
bus.sched: City buses run from early morning to late evening. Nightrider night buses run on weekend nights. Check mobiliteit.lu for times.
tickets: No ticket needed on buses inside Luxembourg
Cross-border RGTR buses: free to the last stop before the border, then a RegioZone ticket
RegioZone ticket: 3 EUR for 2 hours, 5 EUR for a day, valid on buses to neighbouring countries
Saarbrucken Express coach: 5 EUR for 2 hours, 9 EUR for a day
bus.tip: On a cross-border bus, buy your RegioZone ticket before the border. Inspectors check from the last Luxembourg stop.
buy: RegioZone tickets: CFL go app, CFL website, ticket machines and CFL counters
Mobility Centre at Luxembourg station for passes and cross-border tickets

airport.sum: Luxembourg Airport (LUX) at Findel is about 10 km east of the centre. The tram stop Findel - Luxembourg Airport opened on 2 March 2025, and buses 29, 16 and 6 also run to the city. All are free.
airport.sched: From Theater tram stop the tram takes about 16 minutes with a tram every few minutes. Bus 29 from Gare Centrale takes under 22 minutes and runs about every 20 minutes. Lines 16 and 6 run from Hamilius and the city centre.
tickets: Tram and city buses: free, no ticket needed
Regional RGTR buses 223, 302, 361 and 850 also stop at the airport and are free inside Luxembourg
Taxi: charged by meter, rank outside the terminal. Check infotaxi.lu for fares
Train: no station at the airport, the nearest is Luxembourg Gare Centrale
airport.tip: From Gare Centrale, bus 29 is the fastest way. From Kirchberg or the old town, the tram is quicker.
link: Luxembourg Airport: getting to the airport
buy: Tram and bus: nothing to buy
Taxi: from the rank at arrivals, or book at infotaxi.lu
Plan the trip with the Mobiliteit.lu app

metro.note: Luxembourg City has no metro. The Luxtram T1 line, buses and a funicular are all free to use.
lines: Tram T1 runs Stadion - Howald - Gare Centrale - Hamilius - Etoile - Kirchberg - Findel Airport
Gare Centrale: trams, buses and all CFL trains meet here
Hamilius and Place de Metz serve the old town
Philharmonie - Mudam, Europaparlament and Luxexpo are on the Kirchberg section
Findel - Luxembourg Airport is the last stop on the line

tips: Public transport inside Luxembourg is free, but 1st class trains and journeys across the border are not.
Carry an ID card or passport. Inspectors can ask for it, and fines apply on 1st class without a ticket.
The LuxembourgPass is sold for sights and costs 23 EUR for 1 day for one person. It is not needed for transport.
Trains to Trier, Metz and Brussels leave about every hour, so day trips across the border are easy.
